newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Allianz sees 1996 profit up strongly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Allianz sees 1996 profit up strongly.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding on Thursday predicted a strong rise in 1996 profits on the back of careful risk selection, moderate claims development and favourable currency and capital markets.
"The Allianz Group is expecting a further substantial rise in pre-tax profit," the Munich-based market leader said in a statement.
But it cautioned that the rise would not match the 34 percent surge to a record 3.04 billion marks ($1.96 billion) achieved in 1995, which was largely due to a one-off tax break.
Group premium income was up 7.6 percent at 56.2 billion marks at the nine-month stage, boosted by some 1.4 billion marks through foreign currencies' gains against the mark.
Profits were increased by a variety of factors, primarily a more systematic approach to risk selection.

"All things considered, the underwriting result will be higher than last year's figure. Non-underwriting business has benefited from the benign climate on capital markets, making it possible to realise increased gains and investment income has risen," Allianz said.
It added, however, that while its overall investment returns had been favourable, lower interest rates had lowered its returns on new investments in the first nine months of 1996.
Its sales growth had also already been curbed in the first nine months by group restructuring which shaved 200 million marks off premium income.

Allianz this year consolidated its Swiss Berner insurance group and credit insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG while its health insurance unit Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG left the group at the end of July.

The Vereinte health insurance group, which Allianz agreed to take over in full this year in a complicated share swap with reinsurance group Munich Re, will not be consolidated until the start of next year.

Structural changes already impacted on Allianz's 1995 results, when its pre-tax earnings received a major boost from tax benefits associated with its takeover of its East German unit Deutsche Versicherungs AG.

Turning to its worldwide sales development this year, Allianz said its life and health insurance business rose 9.2 percent in the nine-month period, with German life business showing particular improvement.
In addition, single premium variable annuity insurance business resumed its advance in the United States and Italian business also improved.

Non-life business, however, grew just 2.7 percent amid declines on the German, French and Swiss markets, although its British unit Cornhill saw business climb 13.7 percent and its Fireman's Fund in the United States had an 8.9 percent increase in business.
Allianz's German non-life business in particular has been plagued by fierce competition on pricing following the once highly-cartellised market's recent deregulation.
Staff levels dropped by 5.1 percent to 65,500 at September 30, partly due to the group restructuring, without which the decline would have been 4.1 percent.

Allianz said earnings improvements had also been achieved in this area, with personnel and administrative expenses down in the first nine months because of better working procedures and cost control measures.
